research_question: Why did hello become a common greeting, and how did the telephone influence its popularity?

sources.title: Hello: Origin and history
notes: Hello is related to older forms such as hallo, hollo and holla.
Earlier forms were used to attract attention rather than exclusively greet someone.
The word rose in popularity as a greeting with the spread of telephones.

sources.title: Hello, Hello!
notes: The Oxford English Dictionary traces hello through earlier spelling variants.
Older forms could call attention or signal a stop.
The earliest evidence is difficult to establish because spoken use predates dictionaries.

sources.title: Hello
notes: Hello can greet someone, answer a phone or attract attention.
Hullo and hallo are recognised variants.
The word is a late-nineteenth-century variant of older hollo forms.

sources.title: Did 'Hello' Come From Familiar Phone Greeting?
notes: Thomas Edison is often credited with popularising hello on the telephone, but the claim that he was first is unproven.
Hello rose in popularity around the spread of telephones.
Early telephone greeting practices varied by place.

sources.title: Hello: word history and usage
notes: Hello has several related spelling forms in English.
Telephone operators were called hello-girls in the late nineteenth century.
The telephone helped stabilise hello as a familiar opening.
